rows.label: English
rows.description: West Germanic language
rows.hook: became the world's go-to second language for business, science and the internet

rows.label: Spanish
rows.description: Romance language originating in the Iberian Peninsula
rows.hook: is the most spoken native tongue across Latin America, with hundreds of millions of speakers

rows.label: French
rows.description: Romance language
rows.hook: is the language of Paris and is an official tongue on several continents

rows.label: Russian
rows.description: East Slavic language
rows.hook: is written in the Cyrillic alphabet and spoken across the largest country on Earth

rows.label: Persian
rows.description: Western Iranian language
rows.hook: is spoken in Iran and is also called Farsi

rows.label: Hebrew
rows.description: Northwest Semitic language
rows.hook: was revived as an everyday spoken tongue in Israel after centuries as mostly a sacred language

rows.label: Aramaic
rows.description: Semitic language
rows.hook: is thought to be the everyday language spoken by Jesus

rows.label: Arabic
rows.description: Semitic language and lingua franca of the Arab world
rows.hook: is written from right to left and is the language of the Quran

rows.label: Ancient Greek
rows.description: forms of Greek used from around the 9th century BCE to the 6th century CE
rows.hook: was the language of Homer, Plato and Aristotle

rows.label: Catalan
rows.description: Western Romance language
rows.hook: is spoken in Barcelona and the Andorran Pyrenees

rows.label: Mandarin
rows.description: major branch of Chinese spoken across most of northern and southwestern China
rows.hook: is the most widely spoken native language on Earth, with a tonal sound system

rows.label: Indonesian
rows.description: official language of Indonesia
rows.hook: is the national language of an island nation of over 17,000 islands and is written in the Latin alphabet

rows.label: Hungarian
rows.description: Ugric language mainly spoken in Hungary and surrounding countries
rows.hook: is famous for being unrelated to most of its European neighbours and for its many grammatical cases

rows.label: Malay
rows.description: Austronesian macrolanguage, basis for Malaysian Malay and Indonesian
rows.hook: is spoken across Southeast Asia and is the national language of Malaysia and Brunei

rows.label: Punjabi
rows.description: Indo-Aryan language spoken in the Punjab region of Pakistan and India
rows.hook: is the most spoken language of Pakistan and is written in more than one script

rows.label: Thai
rows.description: Tai language
rows.hook: has its own curving alphabet and uses tones to change word meaning

rows.label: Swedish
rows.description: North Germanic language spoken in Sweden and Finland
rows.hook: is the language of IKEA and ABBA

rows.label: Czech
rows.description: West Slavic language
rows.hook: gave the world the word robot

rows.label: Khmer
rows.description: Austroasiatic language of Cambodia
rows.hook: has one of the longest alphabets in the world, with dozens of letters

rows.label: Lithuanian
rows.description: Baltic language spoken in Lithuania
rows.hook: is one of the oldest living European tongues, keeping very archaic features

rows.label: Danish
rows.description: North Germanic language spoken in Northern Europe
rows.hook: is spoken in Copenhagen and has a famously tricky way of pronouncing numbers

rows.label: Norwegian
rows.description: North Germanic language spoken in Norway
rows.hook: is spoken in Oslo and the land of fjords, with two official written standards

rows.label: Bulgarian
rows.description: South Slavic language
rows.hook: is written in Cyrillic, an alphabet first spread by medieval missionaries working in this land

rows.label: Serbian
rows.description: standardized variety of Serbo-Croatian language used by Serbs
rows.hook: is written in both Cyrillic and Latin letters

rows.label: Belarusian
rows.description: East Slavic language
rows.hook: is spoken in Minsk and is written in Cyrillic

rows.label: Galician
rows.description: Western Ibero-Romance language
rows.hook: is spoken in the northwest corner of Spain, near the pilgrim destination Santiago de Compostela

rows.label: Luxembourgish
rows.description: Germanic language or language variety spoken in Luxembourg

rows.label: Macedonian
rows.description: South Slavic language mostly spoken in North Macedonia
rows.hook: is written in a Cyrillic alphabet and spoken around Lake Ohrid and Skopje

rows.label: Javanese
rows.description: Austronesian language
rows.hook: is spoken on the world's most populated island, by tens of millions of people

rows.label: Modern Greek
rows.description: dialects and varieties of the Greek language spoken in the modern era
rows.hook: is written in an alphabet that gave us the words alpha and beta, and is spoken in Athens

rows.label: Latvian
rows.description: Baltic language, official in Latvia and the European Union
rows.hook: is spoken in Riga and is one of only two surviving tongues of its small family

rows.label: Faroese
rows.description: insular Nordic language spoken as a native language by the people of Faroe Islands
rows.hook: is spoken on a remote North Atlantic archipelago of sheep and puffins

rows.label: Slovak
rows.description: West Slavic language spoken in Slovakia
rows.hook: is spoken in Bratislava and is very close to its western neighbour's tongue

rows.label: Cebuano
rows.description: Austronesian language spoken in the Philippines by Cebuanos and other ethnic groups
rows.hook: is widely spoken in the Visayas and southern Philippines, second only to Tagalog-based Filipino
